obs: "It could not have been the intention to throw the whole discussion open ... and to confer upon the tribunals named in the act the power which properly belonged to the political department of the government"
Minnesota Ex Rel. Pearson v. Probate Court of Ramsey County

"Such a definition would not only make the act impracticable of enforcement and, perhaps, unconstitutional in its application, but would also be an unwarranted departure from the accepted meaning of the words defined."

"[T]he potential implications for theforeign relations of the United States of recognizing suchcauses should make courts particularly wary of impingingon the discretion of the Legislative and ExecutiveBranches in managing foreign affairs."

“[T]he Court has taken care to avoid the danger of unwarranted judicial interference in the conduct of foreign policy, and declined to run interference in [the] delicate field of international relations without the affirmative intention of the Congress clearly expressed.”
